title: NY State Assembly · District 41
area: Parts of Borough Park, Midwood, Mapleton and Gravesend in Brooklyn.

context.text: Incumbent Kalman Yeger is running unopposed, appearing on the Republican, Democratic and Conservative Party lines. All three primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled after his only announced opponent, Zahava Durchin, was withdrawn or disqualified from the Democratic and Republican primary ballots.

candidates.name: Kalman Yeger

summary.text: Kalman Yeger is the incumbent for NY State Assembly District 41, elected in November 2024 after eight years on the New York City Council (District 44, 2018-2025). An attorney, he sits on the Aging, Banks, Governmental Employees, Insurance, and Small Business committees and is running for a second term unopposed on the Republican, Democratic and Conservative Party lines.

background.text: Earned an undergraduate degree from Touro College and a J.D. from New York Law School.

Before his 2017 City Council run, worked as senior advisor and counsel to then-Council Member David G. Greenfield and as executive director and counsel for Bronx Borough President Ruben Diaz Jr.'s re-election campaign; also served on Community Board 14 and advised several other city and state officials.
Served on the New York City Council representing District 44 (Borough Park, Midwood, Mapleton, Gravesend) from 2018 to 2025, succeeding David G. Greenfield.
Elected to the Assembly in November 2024, succeeding longtime incumbent Helene Weinstein.

record.text: Serves on the Aging, Banks, Governmental Employees, Insurance, and Small Business committees in the 2025-2026 session.

Sponsored A08970, which would change the deadline for a candidate designated for two or more party nominations to decline a nomination when not chosen in a primary; referred to the Election Law Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A08747 (print no. A08747A), directing the Department of Health to establish an alternative payment methodology for Federally Qualified Health Centers to preserve fertility-care access; amended and recommitted to the Health Committee, and the bill's enacting clause was stricken on March 24, 2026.

Had A11676, prohibiting digital-currency contributions to candidates or political committees, introduced by Rules on his behalf; referred to the Election Law Committee in September 2026, not enacted as of September 2026.

Had A11704, prohibiting municipalities from using adhesive stickers to enforce street parking rules, introduced by Rules on his behalf; referred to the Local Governments Committee in September 2026, not enacted as of September 2026.

A May 2026 Assembly press release credits Yeger and colleagues with securing a state budget provision expanding security funding protections for houses of worship, Jewish schools and community centers amid rising antisemitic harassment.
